title: Feeding Bacteria to House Flies for Microbe Fate and Gene Expression Analysis
author: Dana Nayduch
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.vhde326

steps.title: Collect and sanitize pupae
steps.instruction: Collect pupae from the colony, surface‑sanitize each for 2 min with gentle swirling in 10 % bleach, sterile H₂O, 100 % ethanol, and sterile H₂O (optional, may delay eclosion). Store pupae in a sterile container (e.g., petri dish secured with rubber band or tape) or individually in 15 ml conical tubes until eclosion. Hold at 28 °C (or at room temperature, which slows development by a few days). After eclosion, separate emerged flies from puparia to reduce trans‑stadial bacterial contamination.

steps.title: Prepare fly containers
steps.instruction: Select small petri dishes, 50 ml beakers covered with foil, or small plastic containers with lids (make air holes with a pin). Autoclave or wash to sterilize. Place a ~15 × 15 mm parafilm square at the bottom of each container for the food droplet.

steps.title: Add sterile food droplet and flies
steps.instruction: Prepare a sterile 10 % fly‑food solution or 10 % sucrose droplet of 5–10 µl and pipette onto each parafilm square. Anesthetize newly eclosed 2–3‑day‑old flies with CO₂ or a ~3‑min freezer chill, transfer each fly to a container with soft forceps, and close the lid tightly. The fly will wake, ingest the droplet (flushing gut bacteria and providing sustenance).

steps.title: Fast flies (optional second meal)
steps.instruction: Hold flies at room temperature and fast for 12 h. Optionally, after the first fast, briefly anesthetize with CO₂ or chilling, add a second 10 % sucrose droplet, then fast a second 12 h. Use the same pipettor method for the second droplet.

steps.title: Prepare bacterial seed culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate 100–250 ml of appropriate broth with a single colony of the bacteria of interest. Grow overnight for 8–12 h at the temperature, RPM, and media specified for the strain (do not exceed 12 h to avoid cell death). Use appropriately sized flasks (e.g., 250 ml culture in a 500 ml flask; 100 ml culture in a 250 ml flask).

steps.title: Expand culture to feeding density
steps.instruction: Add 100 µl of the overnight seed culture to ~100 ml sterile broth (volume may vary by species). Incubate at 37 °C with shaking at 200 RPM until the desired OD₆₀₀ is reached. Aim for an OD that yields ~10⁸ CFU/ml so that a 2 µl droplet delivers >10⁵ CFU per fly (minimum 2 × 10⁵ CFU in 2 µl).

steps.title: Feed bacterial droplet
steps.instruction: After the 12 h fast, place the flies in an incubator at 37 °C for ~15 min, then return them to room temperature. Anesthetize if necessary and carefully dispense a 2 µl droplet of the prepared bacterial culture onto the parafilm square. Verify that the full 2 µl has been released from the pipette.

steps.title: Verify ingestion and containment
steps.instruction: Observe flies and mark containers where the entire 2 µl droplet is ingested within 30 min. Discard any flies that ingest partially or after 30 min. For BSL‑2 bacteria, keep infected flies in their primary container inside a secondary container (large bin, cage, etc.) that also allows adequate air circulation.

steps.title: Enumerate fed bacteria
steps.instruction: Serially dilute the stock culture used for feeding (e.g., take 100 µl stock, add to 900 µl sterile media or PBS with appropriate antibiotics) in 1:10 steps. Plate appropriate dilutions on selective agar containing the same antibiotics, incubate at 37 °C for 24 h, and count colonies under a UV lightbox, counting only GFP‑positive colonies.
